title: DaVinci Resolve Pricing: Free vs Studio Cost (2026)
summary: DaVinci Resolve pricing includes free and $295 Studio options with no subscription, so you can choose between the free version or the one-time purchase.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces does about this


Activepieces doesn't touch the Resolve decision, and I'd be suspicious of any tool that claimed to. The Studio question is still the one the checklist above answers: free unless a feature you keep hitting costs you more than $295.


What Activepieces covers is the work around the export. That means


- moving finished files to a client
- requesting approval
- logging the delivery
- chasing the reply


It's easy to ignore when you total up an editor's cost, and it eats unbilled hours.


It's a workflow automation tool where you build flows that connect apps, and the pricing is the part that matters for a cost-conscious editor.


There's no cap on how many flows you can build, on Free at $0 or on any paid plan, so you won't have to restructure workflows to fit budgetary tiers.


Only runs draw on credits: 1,000 a month on Free, and one credit per run however many steps the flow has.


A delivery flow with a dozen steps costs the same as one with two, so you can split delivery, approvals and invoicing reminders into small flows without paying more to keep them tidy.


That's a different shape from the per-action billing elsewhere. Zapier counts a task for each action and Make counts a credit for each module, so a longer chain costs more every time it runs.


For a freelancer billing clients on thin margins, a fixed cost per run is easier to predict than one that grows with every step you add.


The Community Edition is open source under the MIT licence, so if you'd rather keep client files and credentials on your own machine than in someone else's cloud, you can self-host it.


I'd start on Free, wire up one delivery flow after your next export, and see whether the 1,000 monthly runs cover your real volume before paying for anything, which means you'll learn if paid plans are necessary.


For a freelance editor who wants to automate delivery, approvals and invoicing reminders around their exports, Activepieces is the better choice on pricing structure: it never meters how many flows you build, and each run costs one credit however many steps the flow has.


Zapier's per-task and Make's per-module billing make a longer chain cost more every time it runs, which is a fair model for some users but harder to budget on thin margins.


It won't change the Resolve Studio decision, but for the work around the export, a flat cost per run lets you split things into small, tidy flows without paying more for it.
